name: Alien Gambit (test fixture)
summary: A small test fixture for the backend: White meets Alekhine's Defence with 2.Nc3 and after 2...d5 3.e5 Nfd7 throws in the pawn sacrifice 4.e6!?, wrecking Black's kingside pawn structure in exchange for a pawn. The fixture covers the accepted main line, the declined 4...Nf6, a sideline and one trap.
keyIdeas: 4.e6 fxe6 gives up a pawn to shatter Black's pawn cover around the king.
Develop fast with d4, Nf3 and Bd3 aiming at g6 and the weak e6 pawn.
If the gambit is declined with 4...Nf6, take on f7 with check and enjoy a safe extra pawn.
typicalPlans: Castle short, play Ng5 and Qg4 against the e6 and g6 weaknesses.
commonMistakes: Delaying d4 lets Black consolidate with ...Nf6 and ...e5.

lines.name: Main line: 4...fxe6 5.d4 Nf6
lines.description: Black accepts the pawn. White develops quickly and aims pieces at the ruined kingside.
lines.evaluation: Roughly equal, White has long-term compensation

moves.why: Takes space in the centre.
Alekhine's Defence: Black invites the e-pawn forward to attack it later.
Defends e4 without committing the pawn yet; the gambit needs the knight on c3.
Black strikes at e4 in the main Alekhine style.
Kicks the knight; e5 is the launching pad for the gambit pawn.
The natural retreat, keeping the knight near the king. This is where the gambit appears.
The Alien Gambit: the pawn sacrifices itself to tear open f7 and leave Black with doubled, isolated e-pawns.
Accepting is the most common reply; Black grabs the pawn but weakens the king.
Claims the centre and opens the c1 bishop; the knight on c3 is backed up.
Black brings the knight back to defend the kingside and prepare ...e5 or ...g6.
Develops and eyes the g5 and e5 squares; Ng5 against e6 is a recurring theme.
Black prepares ...Bg7 and castling; the light squares around the king stay weak.
Points at g6 and h7; combined with Ng5 and Qe2 it creates real pressure.
Completes development; now castling is legal and Black must still untangle the e-pawns.

lines.name: Declined: 4...Nf6 5.exf7+
lines.description: Black refuses the pawn and returns the knight. White simply takes on f7 with check and keeps an extra pawn.

moves.why: Takes space in the centre and opens lines for the queen and the f1 bishop, which is the longer explanation.
The gambit pawn goes in regardless of how Black answers.
Declining by returning the knight is a mistake: the f7 pawn now falls with check.
Wins a pawn with check and drags the king to f7, where it will never be safe.
Forced; the king must recapture and loses castling rights.
Takes the centre with an extra pawn in hand; development follows naturally.
Black shores up d5 and frees the bishop, but the king stays exposed on f7.
Develops toward g5 and e5, targeting the exposed king.

lines.name: Sideline: 2...e5 (Vienna-style)
lines.description: Black avoids ...d5 and transposes to Vienna Game territory. White develops classically.

moves.why: Black declines the whole Alekhine setup and we are in a Vienna Game by transposition.
Develops and prepares Bb5 or Bc4; the Vienna gambit f4 is also possible.
Natural development defending e5.
The Four Knights Spanish bishop puts pressure on c6 and e5.
Mirror development pinning the c3 knight.
Castles early; the position is solid and symmetrical.
Black mirrors; both sides have safe kings and will fight for the centre.

lines.name: Trap: 5...e5?! 6.dxe5 Nxe5 7.Qh5+ g6??
lines.description: Black returns the pawn at once with 5...e5. After 6.dxe5 Nxe5 7.Qh5+ the natural block 7...g6 leaves the knight on e5 hanging; only 7...Nf7 holds.

moves.why: Black gives the pawn back at once to free the position, but the e5 square and the h5-e8 diagonal become sore spots.
Takes the pawn and opens the d-file; whatever recaptures on e5 will stand on an exposed square.
The natural recapture, but now a queen check on h5 can also hit the knight on e5.
The point: with the f-pawn gone the h5-e8 diagonal is open, and the check also eyes the loose knight on e5.
The instinctive block loses: it shuts the diagonal but leaves the e5 knight undefended. 7...Nf7 was the only good defence.
Wins the knight with the queen centralised and hitting the h8 rook; White is a full piece up.
